sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
I'm Shankar Vedanta.
Maybe your mornings sound like this.
sentences.zh: 也许你的早晨是这样开始的。

sentences.en: You wake up to your alarm ringing, you turn it off, and bring your phone back to bed with you.
sentences.zh: 闹钟响了，你醒来，关掉闹钟，然后把手机带回床上。

sentences.en: You scroll through email and social media, squinting through one eye to see what you've got to get done and what's happening in the news.
sentences.zh: 你刷着邮件和社交媒体，眯着一只眼看自己有哪些事要做，以及新闻里发生了什么。

sentences.en: When you finally get up and start getting ready, maybe you have some music going, or your favorite TV channel.
sentences.zh: 当你终于起床开始准备时，也许会放点音乐，或者打开你最喜欢的电视频道。

sentences.en: And we continue to follow that breaking news in South Shore.
sentences.zh: 我们将继续关注南岸的突发新闻。

sentences.en: Many of us are voracious consumers of information, and we're always looking for new ways to take in even more.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人都是贪婪的信息消费者，总是在寻找获取更多信息的新途径。

sentences.en: Alexa, what's the weather today?
In Charlotte, North Carolina, it's 63 degrees with mostly sunny skies.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州夏洛特市，气温63度，大部分时间是晴天。

sentences.en: But even as we savor good news about the weather or the stock market or weekend plans, we're also regularly confronted by stuff that's unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 但即使我们在享受关于天气、股市或周末计划的好消息时，也经常会面对一些令人不快的事情。

sentences.en: To listen to your unread voicemails, press 1.
sentences.zh: 收听未读语音留言，请按1。

sentences.en: Unpleasant information creates a paradox for the brain.
sentences.zh: 令人不快的信息给大脑制造了一个悖论。

sentences.en: This kind of information is often very important.
sentences.zh: 这类信息往往非常重要。

sentences.en: First message.
This is the principal calling from your son's school.
sentences.zh: 我是你儿子学校的校长。

sentences.en: Please contact us so we can arrange a time to discuss your son's behavior.
sentences.zh: 请联系我们，以便我们安排时间讨论你儿子的行为问题。

sentences.en: But this kind of information also produces psychic pain.
sentences.zh: 但这类信息也会产生心理痛苦。

sentences.en: And one of the oldest rules in the brain is to avoid things that are painful.
sentences.zh: 大脑最古老的法则之一就是避开痛苦的事物。

sentences.en: Second message.
This is the doctor's office.
Your test results have come in.
Please call us back immediately.
The tension between what we rationally know to be important and what we emotionally experience as painful is the subject of our episode today.
sentences.zh: 我们理性上认为重要的事情与情感上体验到的痛苦之间的张力，就是我们今天这期节目的主题。

sentences.en: Third message.
Hey, just call me back to get this.
sentences.zh: 嘿，回我个电话，听听这个。

sentences.en: I saw your wife kissing somebody.
sentences.zh: 我看到你妻子在亲吻别人。

sentences.en: Sorry.
Just give me a call.
It's about why we sometimes...
sentences.zh: 这是关于为什么我们有时……

sentences.en: Message deleted.
Message deleted.
Shut it all out.
Why we look away, and the consequences of doing so, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会选择回避，以及这样做的后果，本周《隐藏的大脑》为您揭晓。

sentences.en: There's an old theory in economics about information.
sentences.zh: 经济学中有一个关于信息的古老理论。

sentences.en: It goes like this.
You should always be willing to hear information about your finances or your health.
sentences.zh: 你应该总是愿意听取关于你财务或健康的信息。

sentences.en: For example...
Hey, Antonio.
Help yourself to anything in the fridge but, heads up, sniff the milk firSt.
sentences.zh: 冰箱里的东西随便吃，但提醒一下，先闻闻牛奶。

sentences.en: I think it's getting close to the expiration date.
Maybe this information is useful.
sentences.zh: 也许这个信息是有用的。

sentences.en: Maybe it's not.
Oh, I'm fine.
I'm actually lactose intolerant.
No matter how you feel about the information, there's one thing you should never do.
sentences.zh: 无论你对这些信息感觉如何，有一件事你永远不该做。

sentences.en: A person should never avoid information because information can never hurt a decision.
sentences.zh: 一个人永远不应该回避信息，因为信息绝不会损害决策。

sentences.en: This is Josh Tassoff.
I'm an assistant professor of economics at Claremont Graduate University.
sentences.zh: 我是克莱蒙特研究生大学的经济学助理教授。

sentences.en: Josh says less is never more when it comes to information.
sentences.zh: 乔什说，在信息方面，少绝不是多。

sentences.en: We always should want to know if our 401k is about to take a nosedive or if we're at risk of contracting a disease.
sentences.zh: 我们总是应该想知道我们的401k退休金账户是否即将暴跌，或者我们是否有患病的风险。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
Humans aren't always rational.
And when it comes to information...
Information can be anxiety-provoking.
It could be depressing.
What do we do when something makes us sad or depressed?
sentences.zh: 当某件事让我们感到悲伤或沮丧时，我们会怎么做？

sentences.en: We turn away from it.
When the thing that's depressing is information, we say,
sentences.zh: 当令人沮丧的东西是信息时，我们会说：

sentences.en: I don't want to hear about it.
Social scientists call this behavior information aversion.
sentences.zh: 社会科学家称这种行为为“信息厌恶”。

sentences.en: More commonly, it's called the ostrich effect.
sentences.zh: 更常见的说法是“鸵鸟效应”。

sentences.en: The term comes not from birds, but investors.
sentences.zh: 这个词不是来自鸟类，而是来自投资者。

sentences.en: So when the stock market goes down, people check their portfolio less frequently than when the stock market is going up.
sentences.zh: 所以当股市下跌时，人们查看投资组合的频率比股市上涨时要低。

sentences.en: And why would that be?
Well, the interpretation is that the information causes sort of an immediate pain just from hearing it, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，解释是，信息仅仅在被听到时就会产生一种即时的痛苦，对吧？

sentences.en: People are anticipating sort of their future losses.
sentences.zh: 人们在预见他们未来的损失。

sentences.en: Of course, they don't actually have any losses yet, but they're anticipating those future losses,
sentences.zh: 当然，他们实际上还没有任何损失，但他们预见了那些未来的损失，

sentences.en: and that causes an emotional pain obtaining that information.
sentences.zh: 而获取这些信息会造成情感上的痛苦。

sentences.en: Information aversion is one of many, many domains where human behavior seems to deviate from the models of economists.
sentences.zh: 信息厌恶是人类行为似乎偏离经济学家模型的多重领域之一。

sentences.en: Instead of doing the rational thing, learning as much as possible about something,
sentences.zh: 我们许多人没有做理性的事情，即尽可能多地了解某事，

sentences.en: many of us do the opposite.
We stick our heads in the sand.
And this is true for more than just financial information.
sentences.zh: 这不仅适用于财务信息。

sentences.en: A couple of months ago, we asked Hidden Brain listeners to call in and tell us about their news consumption.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，我们请《隐藏的大脑》的听众打来电话，告诉我们他们的资讯消费情况。

sentences.en: Hi, Annie here.
Hello, my name is Nancy Walter.
Hi, Shaka, this is Jason Flakes.
sentences.zh: 嗨，尚卡尔，我是杰森·弗莱克斯。

sentences.en: Jason, Nancy, and Annie are all addicted to the news.
sentences.zh: 杰森、南希和安妮都是新闻成瘾者。

sentences.en: My husband and I are news junkies.
sentences.zh: 我和我丈夫都是新闻迷。

sentences.en: I love listening to the news every day.
Checking it every few hours.
sentences.zh: 每隔几个小时就查看一次。

sentences.en: Or at least, they were addicted to the news until Donald Trump caught them by surprise and won the 2016 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 或者至少，在唐纳德·特朗普出人意料地赢得2016年总统大选之前，他们是新闻成瘾者。

sentences.en: I hadn't anticipated Donald Trump winning.
sentences.zh: 我没预料到唐纳德·特朗普会赢。

sentences.en: So I went on a complete news blackout.
sentences.zh: 所以我完全切断了新闻来源。

sentences.en: Just because of the frustration that I was feeling.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为我感到的挫败感。

sentences.en: And actually had a lot of anxiety because of it.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上因此感到非常焦虑。

sentences.en: I have dramatically changed the way I read the news following the election.
sentences.zh: 选举后，我彻底改变了阅读新闻的方式。

sentences.en: These listeners had their fingers on the pulse of political news before the election,
sentences.zh: 在选举前，当希拉里·克林顿看起来胜券在握时，这些听众对政治新闻了如指掌，

sentences.en: when Hillary Clinton appeared to be poised for victory.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普意外获胜后的几天和几周里，

sentences.en: But in the days and weeks after Trump's surprising win,
sentences.zh: 杰森、南希和安妮开始回避新闻。

sentences.en: Jason, Nancy, and Annie began to avoid the news.
sentences.zh: 这就像那些在股市上涨时深情注视着自己投资组合，

sentences.en: It was like the investors who stare lovingly at their portfolios when the stock market's on the rise,
sentences.zh: 但只要市场下跌就避免查看的投资者一样。

sentences.en: but avoid looking whenever the market dips.
sentences.zh: 关于特朗普政府的头条新闻让这些听众感到压力。

sentences.en: Headlines about the Trump administration stress these listeners out.
It caused them pain.
sentences.zh: 而这正是信息厌恶的一个关键标志。

sentences.en: And that's a key marker of information aversion.
sentences.zh: 现在，有时人们回避信息是因为它实在难以消化。

sentences.en: Now, there are times when people avoid information when it's simply too much to digeSt.
sentences.zh: 假设你正在为一场大考学习，

sentences.en: Let's say you're studying for a big test,
sentences.zh: 在阅读了几个小时之后，

sentences.en: and after hours and hours of reading,
you close your textbooks and take a break.
This is information overload.
sentences.zh: 你因为摄入太多东西而精疲力竭。

sentences.en: You're burnt out from taking in so much stuff.
sentences.zh: 对于信息厌恶，驱动因素不是信息太多。

sentences.en: With information aversion, the driver isn't that there's too much information.
It's that the information is unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 如果你告诉这些人一些令人愉快的事情，

sentences.en: If you were to tell these people about pleasant things,
sentences.zh: 他们会很乐意听上一整天。

sentences.en: they'd be glad to listen all day.
sentences.zh: 人们想要信息，想要更多关于未来快乐经历的信息，

sentences.en: People want information, want more information about happier future experiences
sentences.zh: 而不是关于未来不那么快乐经历的信息。

sentences.en: than less happy future experiences.
sentences.zh: 乔什想看看人们在多大程度上更喜欢快乐的信息而不是不愉快的信息。

sentences.en: Josh wanted to see how much people prefer happy information to unpleasant information.
sentences.zh: 他想测试那个古老的理论。

sentences.en: He wanted to test that age-old theory.
sentences.zh: 你应该总是愿意听取关于你财务或健康的信息。

sentences.en: You should always be willing to hear information about your finances or your health.
sentences.zh: 于是他与一位同事合作。

sentences.en: So he teamed up with a colleague.
I'm Ananda Ganguly.
sentences.zh: 我在克莱蒙特麦肯纳学院。

sentences.en: I'm at Claremont McKenna College.
sentences.zh: 他们请参与者进来，坐在桌子前20分钟。

sentences.en: And they asked participants to come in and sit at a desk for 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 在他们面前的隔间里贴着两个信封，

sentences.en: And posted at their cubicle in front of them were two envelopes,
sentences.zh: 一个标着“大”，一个标着“小”。

sentences.en: one labeled big and one labeled small.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉志愿者，信封里装有现金的几率为10%。

sentences.en: They told the volunteers that there was a 10% chance the envelopes were filled with cash.
sentences.zh: 但如果大信封里有钱，里面就是100美元。

sentences.en: But if the big envelope contains money, it contains $100.
sentences.zh: 如果小信封里有钱，里面就是10美元。

sentences.en: If the small envelope contains money, it contains $10.
sentences.zh: 志愿者可以在20分钟结束时打开信封，把里面的钱装进兜里。

sentences.en: The volunteers would get to open the envelopes at the end of 20 minutes and pocket the contents.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果20分钟太长等不及，

sentences.en: Now, if 20 minutes was too long to wait,
sentences.zh: 乔什和阿南达说，志愿者可以付钱立即打开其中一个信封。

sentences.en: Josh and Ananda said the volunteers could pay money to open one of the envelopes immediately.
83.4% paid money to affect the timing.
sentences.zh: 你真的亲眼观察了这些志愿者吗？

sentences.en: Did you actually physically observe the volunteers?
sentences.zh: 在他们处理这件事时，你注意到了什么吗？

sentences.en: Did you notice anything as they were dealing with this?
sentences.zh: 你能真的看到他们脸上的纠结吗？

sentences.en: Could you actually see the dilemma on their faces?
Yeah, they were in the computer.
sentences.zh: 他们在计算机实验室里做这件事。

sentences.en: They were in a computer lab and doing this.
sentences.zh: 绝对可以，我的意思是，这几乎就像在赌场里一样。

sentences.en: And absolutely, I mean, it was almost like in a casino.
sentences.zh: 但他们会立即开始撕开信封。

sentences.en: But immediately, they would start tearing the envelopes open.
sentences.zh: 而且我立刻就对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And immediately, I'm very excited about it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，脏话会脱口而出。

sentences.en: And, you know, F-words would fly.
sentences.zh: 那么脏话是在他们打开信封后还是之前脱口而出的？

sentences.en: And would F-words fly once they'd opened the envelopes or before?
After they opened the envelopes.
It's the disappointment or the surprise.
Here's the trick in the experiment.
Remember that there were two envelopes.
One big, one small.
sentences.zh: 大信封有获得大笔钱的潜力。

sentences.en: Big envelopes carry the potential of a big sum of money.
sentences.zh: 小信封有获得小笔钱的潜力。

sentences.en: Small envelopes carry the potential of a small sum of money.
sentences.zh: 你可以猜到志愿者想打开哪一个。

sentences.en: You can guess which ones the volunteers wanted to open.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们打开大信封的几率是打开小信封的两倍。

sentences.en: What we find is that people are twice as likely to open up the big envelope over the small envelope.
sentences.zh: 解释是，赢得100美元比赢得10美元要快乐得多，也令人兴奋得多。

sentences.en: The interpretation is that winning $100 is a lot more happy and a lot more exciting than winning $10.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们对这些信息的需求，即使它在决策中完全没用，也要高得多。

sentences.en: And so people's demand for that information, even though it's completely useless in their decision making, is much higher.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我完全跟上了。

sentences.en: I'm not sure I fully followed that.
Walk me through that again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里的信息对于做任何决定都是完全没用的。

sentences.en: Well, the information here is completely useless for making any decisions.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，他们要么会得到这笔钱，要么得不到，对吧？

sentences.en: So no matter what, they're going to get this money or not get the money, right?
They're just going to sit there for 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他们只是要在那里坐上20分钟。

sentences.en: And so receiving this information, unlike other decisions in our life, like you could think in our daily life, if you're going to get a raise or anything like this,
sentences.zh: 所以，接收这些信息与我们生活中的其他决定不同，比如你可以想想在日常生活中，如果你要涨工资或类似的事情，

sentences.en: that information can be very useful because it'll help you improve your purchase decisions right now in the present.
sentences.zh: 这些信息可能非常有用，因为它能帮助你改善当下的购买决策。

sentences.en: But here, they're basically stuck sitting in the lab in a seat.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，他们基本上只能被困在实验室的座位上。

sentences.en: And so receiving this information 20 minutes earlier is completely useless.
sentences.zh: 因此，提前20分钟收到这些信息完全没用。

sentences.en: They can't use it to improve any decisions in that short interim period.
sentences.zh: 在那么短的间隔期内，他们无法利用这些信息来改善任何决策。

sentences.en: Even if receiving the information earlier was useless, lots of volunteers were perfectly willing to pay to find out what was inside the envelope sooner.
sentences.zh: 即使提前收到信息毫无用处，许多志愿者也非常愿意花钱来尽早知道信封里装的是什么。

sentences.en: The bigger the potential good news, the more likely volunteers were to pay.
sentences.zh: 潜在的好消息越大，志愿者付费的可能性就越高。

sentences.en: The study showed that people are hungry for information when information is pleasant.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，当信息令人愉悦时，人们对信息非常渴望。

sentences.en: Now, there's one important detail we haven't told you yet.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一个重要的细节我们还没告诉你。

sentences.en: The amount the volunteers had to pay wasn't very much, just 50 cents to open an envelope.
sentences.zh: 志愿者需要支付的金额并不多，打开一个信封只需50美分。

sentences.en: Since the big envelope could hold as much as $100, you might say that paying 50 cents was a trivial coSt.
sentences.zh: 由于大信封里最多可能有100美元，你可能会说支付50美分是微不足道的成本。

sentences.en: We wanted to look at something that had greater real-world stakes.
sentences.zh: 我们想研究一些在现实世界中影响更大的事情。

sentences.en: We know people want pleasant information.
sentences.zh: 我们知道人们想要令人愉悦的信息。

sentences.en: But are they willing to pay to avoid unpleasant news, like information about a disease?
sentences.zh: 但他们是否愿意花钱去避免不愉快的新闻，比如关于某种疾病的信息？

sentences.en: Josh and Ananda decided to find out.
They thought about the health concerns you might see on a college campus.
sentences.zh: 他们想到了你在大学校园里可能会看到的健康问题。

sentences.en: The sample that we have access to are college undergrads, right?
sentences.zh: 我们能接触到的样本是大学本科生，对吧？

sentences.en: And so we could do something like a cancer test, but I don't think college undergrads are terribly concerned about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以做类似癌症测试的事情，但我认为大学生对此并不太担心。

sentences.en: I think what college undergrads tend to be typically concerned about is STDs.
sentences.zh: 我认为大学生通常比较担心的是性传播疾病。

sentences.en: STDs, sexually transmitted diseases.
One of the most stigmatized and common diseases on college campuses is herpes.
sentences.zh: 在大学校园里，最受歧视且最常见的疾病之一是疱疹。

sentences.en: It's caused by the herpes simplex virus, or HSV.
sentences.zh: 它是由单纯疱疹病毒（HSV）引起的。

sentences.en: We chose HSV because the prevalence, the rate of prevalence of HSV in this population is rather high.
sentences.zh: 我们选择HSV是因为这种病毒在这一人群中的流行率相当高。

sentences.en: I mean, rough numbers are around 50%.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，粗略估计在50%左右。

sentences.en: Chances are every other person has it, so they would have it.
sentences.zh: 很有可能每两个人中就有一个人携带，所以他们可能会感染。

sentences.en: And then the other attractive thing about HSV for us is it had this kind of two levels, kind of parallel, a $10 and $100 thing.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，HSV的另一个吸引力在于它有两个层面，类似于10美元和100美元的对比。

sentences.en: There's herpes simplex virus 1 and herpes simplex virus 2.
sentences.zh: 有单纯疱疹病毒1型和单纯疱疹病毒2型。

sentences.en: Herpes simplex virus 1 is typically associated with cold sores.
sentences.zh: 单纯疱疹病毒1型通常与唇疱疹有关。

sentences.en: And herpes simplex virus 2 is typically associated with genital herpes.
sentences.zh: 而单纯疱疹病毒2型通常与生殖器疱疹有关。

sentences.en: HSV 1, that's the oral herpes, is less considered to be less severe or less stigmatic or whatever in the population.
sentences.zh: HSV 1，也就是口腔疱疹，在人群中被认为不那么严重，或者说没那么受歧视。

sentences.en: Ananda and Josh asked college students to come back to their lab.
sentences.zh: Ananda和Josh请大学生回到他们的实验室。

sentences.en: This time, volunteers were asked to sit through a webinar about herpes.
sentences.zh: 这一次，志愿者被要求参加一场关于疱疹的网络研讨会。

sentences.en: We actually give them photographs of sores on the lips and photographs of sores on male and female genitalia with a discussion of HSV 1 and HSV 2.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上给他们看了嘴唇上溃疡的照片，以及男性和女性生殖器上溃疡的照片，并讨论了HSV 1和HSV 2。

sentences.en: And these pictures were graphic?
These pictures were very graphic.
In fact, we don't know that we'll be able, we'll want to put it in the paper.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们不知道是否能把它们放进论文里。

sentences.en: They were completely clinical graphic.
sentences.zh: 它们是完全临床化的写实照片。

sentences.en: Since Josh and Ananda knew that some people avoid getting tested for herpes because they don't want to deal with a blood test,
sentences.zh: 由于Josh和Ananda知道有些人因为不想面对抽血检查而避免进行疱疹检测，

sentences.en: volunteers were told they had to have their blood drawn in order to stay in the study.
sentences.zh: 志愿者被告知必须抽血才能留在研究中。

sentences.en: The researchers told volunteers they could have the blood tested for free for both kinds of herpes.
sentences.zh: 研究人员告诉志愿者，他们可以免费检测这两种疱疹。

sentences.en: Volunteers were assured confidentiality.
sentences.zh: 志愿者被保证了保密性。

sentences.en: They were allowed to call into the lab with their initials and four randomly selected numbers of their own choice.
sentences.zh: 他们可以拨打实验室电话，报上自己的姓名首字母和四个自选的随机数字。

sentences.en: Even the doctor would not know who they were.
sentences.zh: 即使是医生也不会知道他们是谁。

sentences.en: So, to recap, students were given graphic information about two forms of herpes.
sentences.zh: 所以，回顾一下，学生们获得了关于两种疱疹形式的写实信息。

sentences.en: The researchers then proceeded to eliminate all the usual reasons someone might not want to get tested for the sexually transmitted disease.
sentences.zh: 研究人员随后排除了人们不想检测性传播疾病的所有常见原因。

sentences.en: It was mandatory for the volunteers to get their blood drawn, the test was free, and the results would be obtained confidentially.
sentences.zh: 志愿者必须抽血是强制性的，检测是免费的，结果也会保密。

sentences.en: Would volunteers elect to find out if they had herpes?
sentences.zh: 志愿者会选择去了解自己是否患有疱疹吗？

sentences.en: Or would they choose to bury their heads in the sand?
sentences.zh: 还是他们会选择掩耳盗铃？

sentences.en: To test for information aversion, the researchers told the volunteers that they would have to pay $10 to not get their blood tested.
sentences.zh: 为了测试信息厌恶，研究人员告诉志愿者，他们必须支付10美元才能不进行血液检测。

sentences.en: A significant number of volunteers elected to pay this money.
sentences.zh: 相当一部分志愿者选择了支付这笔钱。

sentences.en: And just as the researchers had expected,
sentences.zh: 正如研究人员所预料的那样，

sentences.en: volunteers were more likely to pay money to avoid getting highly unpleasant information about genital herpes than the less unpleasant information about oral herpes.
sentences.zh: 志愿者更愿意花钱去避免获取关于生殖器疱疹的高度不愉快信息，而不是关于口腔疱疹的不那么令人不快的信息。

sentences.en: Tell me about those people.
So, they just sat, did that happen in front of them, or how did that happen?
sentences.zh: 所以，他们只是坐在那里，那是当着他们的面发生的吗，还是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So, the phlebotomist drew the blood, and we said, okay, so this was your choice.
sentences.zh: 抽血员抽了血，我们说，好吧，这是你的选择。

sentences.en: You had chosen not to be tested, so now this blood would be discarded.
sentences.zh: 你选择了不进行检测，所以现在这些血会被丢弃。

sentences.en: Would you please drop it down the sink and wash it out?
sentences.zh: 请你把它倒进水槽并冲掉好吗？

sentences.en: And they did?
They did.
They would drop the tube into the sink and turn on the faucet, and it would fill.
sentences.zh: 他们会把试管扔进水槽，打开水龙头，水就会溢出来。

sentences.en: I mean, at some level, that has to be a little bit disturbing, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种程度上，这一定有点令人不安，对吧？

sentences.en: The idea that you're drawing blood and throwing it down the sink?
sentences.zh: 抽了血却把它倒进水槽的想法？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
And that's kind of the point here, though.
sentences.zh: 但这正是这里的关键所在。

sentences.en: So, they are going to have the blood drawn.
So, you'd rather pay money, waste that blood, than know what your test results were.
sentences.zh: 所以，你宁愿花钱、浪费那些血，也不愿知道你的检测结果。

sentences.en: Did any of the students give you verbal feedback about what happened and their impressions of it?
sentences.zh: 有没有学生对发生的事情以及他们的印象给出过口头反馈？

sentences.en: Did any of them explain why they declined to be tested?
sentences.zh: 有没有人解释他们为什么拒绝检测？

sentences.en: I mean, they obviously must have thought about what the implications were as they made the choice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在做出选择时显然一定考虑过其中的含义。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
So, yeah, we actually asked them, what was your motivation?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们确实问过他们，你的动机是什么？

sentences.en: 85.7%, the most common explanation, was because, quote,
sentences.zh: 85.7%的人给出的最常见解释是，引用原话：

sentences.en: it will cause me unnecessary stress or anxiety if I test positive.
sentences.zh: “如果检测结果呈阳性，会给我带来不必要的压力或焦虑。”

sentences.en: It's worth pointing out that lots of students elected to receive the information about whether they had herpes.
sentences.zh: 值得指出的是，许多学生还是选择了接收关于他们是否患有疱疹的信息。

sentences.en: In fact, a majority of students elected to do the rational thing and get their blood tested.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数学生选择了理性的做法，进行了血液检测。

sentences.en: But that isn't surprising.
The surprising thing is that that number wasn't 100% because...
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是这个数字不是100%，因为……

sentences.en: You should always be willing to hear information about your finances or your health.
sentences.zh: 你应该总是愿意了解关于你的财务或健康状况的信息。

sentences.en: As many as 20% of the students were willing to pay cold, hard cash to avoid finding out that they had genital herpes.
sentences.zh: 多达20%的学生愿意支付真金白银来避免发现自己患有生殖器疱疹。

sentences.en: Another thing the researchers found, students who were in a good mood were more likely to avoid information than those in a bad mood.
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现的另一件事是，心情好的学生比心情差的学生更容易回避信息。

sentences.en: This may seem surprising, but it actually makes complete sense.
sentences.zh: 这看起来可能令人惊讶，但实际上完全讲得通。

sentences.en: When you're in a good mood, do you really want to ruin how you feel by discovering you have herpes?
sentences.zh: 当你心情好的时候，你真的想通过发现自己患有疱疹来破坏这种感觉吗？

sentences.en: It's like an ignorance is bliss result.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种“无知即幸福”的结果。

sentences.en: Think for a moment about the implications of information aversion.
sentences.zh: 花点时间思考一下信息厌恶的含义。

sentences.en: So many health and well-being messages are premised on the idea that people will act rationally when it comes to preserving their health.
sentences.zh: 许多关于健康和福祉的信息都基于这样一个前提：人们在维护自身健康时会表现得理性。

sentences.en: What if that isn't true for a sizable number of people?
sentences.zh: 如果这对相当多的人来说不是真的呢？

sentences.en: I think that we should consider whether scare tactics in advertising and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该考虑广告中的恐吓策略之类的方法。

sentences.en: I mean, whether that is a good technique to encourage people to get tested or not is questionable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是否是鼓励人们进行检测的好方法，值得怀疑。

sentences.en: When we come back, we're going to leave the lab and head out into the real world to see how information aversion plays out in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将离开实验室，走进现实世界，看看信息厌恶在日常生活中是如何体现的。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
This is Hidden Brain.
I'm Shankar Vedantam.
There's no question that fear is an effective way to change how people behave.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，恐惧是改变人们行为的有效方式。

sentences.en: When a parent tells a kid to fall in line or risk losing iPad privileges for a week,
sentences.zh: 当父母告诉孩子要听话，否则可能会失去一周玩iPad的权利时，

sentences.en: or when a boss tells an employee to come into work on time or risk getting fired,
sentences.zh: 或者当老板告诉员工要准时上班，否则可能会被解雇时，

sentences.en: these often produce the desired effect.
sentences.zh: 这些通常会产生预期的效果。

sentences.en: We use scare tactics in public service announcements all the time,
sentences.zh: 我们在公共服务公告中一直使用恐吓策略，

sentences.en: like in this road safety commercial from Thailand,
sentences.zh: 比如泰国这个道路安全广告，

sentences.en: where a speeding car runs into a group of pedestrians,
sentences.zh: 一辆超速行驶的汽车撞向了一群行人，

sentences.en: or this anti-smoking advertisement from Poland,
sentences.zh: 或者波兰这个反吸烟广告，

sentences.en: where a lit cigarette is transformed into a candle at the base of a tombstone.
sentences.zh: 一支点燃的香烟在墓碑底部变成了一支蜡烛。

sentences.en: In Josh and Ananda's study, the majority of volunteers chose to get tested
sentences.zh: 在Josh和Ananda的研究中，大多数志愿者在接触到疱疹的写实图像后，

sentences.en: after being exposed to graphic images of herpes.
This makes sense, says University of Illinois psychology professor Dolores Albaracen.
sentences.zh: 伊利诺伊大学心理学教授Dolores Albaracen说，这很有道理。

sentences.en: If you induce a significant level of fear,
sentences.zh: 如果你诱发了相当程度的恐惧，

sentences.en: you're going to get a comparable reaction on the behavioral side.
sentences.zh: 你在行为方面就会得到相应的反应。

sentences.en: Dolores and a team of researchers analyzed 250 studies done
sentences.zh: Dolores和一组研究人员分析了250项关于恐惧在改变行为方面有效性的研究。

sentences.en: about the effectiveness of fear in transforming behavior.
sentences.zh: 虽然研究表明恐惧确实有效，

sentences.en: While the research shows fear indeed is effective,
Dolores says it has limitations.
sentences.zh: 它对一次性行为确实更有效。

sentences.en: It does work better for one-time behavior.
So getting vaccinated,
sentences.zh: 如果我面临威胁，并且之后有有效的疫苗，

sentences.en: if I have a threat and there is an effective vaccine right after,
and I just go in and get it one time,
that's easy to do.
sentences.zh: 行为在你体验到情绪后立即完成。

sentences.en: The behavior is done right after you experience the emotion.
Emotions are not that long-lasting,
so it's going to have an effect.
sentences.zh: 但如果涉及到遵循正确的饮食习惯，

sentences.en: But if it comes down to following the right diet,
we all know how difficult that is.
sentences.zh: 而且你在某一时刻感受到的任何恐惧，第二天就消失了。

sentences.en: And whatever fear you might experience at one point is gone the next day.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题的症结所在。

sentences.en: This is the crux of the issue.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让某人做一次某事，

sentences.en: If you want someone to do something one time,
sentences.zh: 用恐惧来促使他们去做可能非常有效。

sentences.en: frightening them into doing it could be very effective.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想让他们定期做某事，

sentences.en: But if you want them to do something regularly
sentences.zh: 并且是在很长一段时间内，

sentences.en: and over a long period of time,
fear might not be effective.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些研究表明它可能会适得其反。

sentences.en: In fact, some research suggests it could be counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 如果你不介意的话，让我先请你，

sentences.en: Let me just have you start, if you don't mind,
sentences.zh: 先做个自我介绍，告诉我你的名字。

sentences.en: by just introducing yourself and tell me your name.
Sure.
My name is Ritesh Banerjee.
I'm an economiSt.
A few years ago, Ritesh and his colleague,
sentences.zh: 几年前，里特什和他的同事

sentences.en: Giulio Zanella,
sentences.zh: 开始研究3000名美国女性的数据，

sentences.en: began looking at data about 3,000 American women
sentences.zh: 她们都在一家大公司工作。

sentences.en: who all worked at a large company.
sentences.zh: 所有女性的年龄都在50到64岁之间，

sentences.en: All the women were between the ages of 50 and 64,
sentences.zh: 她们都参加了一项保险计划，

sentences.en: and they were all covered by an insurance plan
sentences.zh: 该计划每年提供一次免费的乳房X光检查。

sentences.en: that provided a free mammogram every year.
sentences.zh: 这被认为是抗击乳腺癌的重要工具。

sentences.en: Which is perceived to be an important tool
sentences.zh: 这家公司确实大力推动帮助女性

sentences.en: in the fight against breast cancer.
This company made a real push to help women
sentences.zh: 它会自动为员工安排乳房X光检查，

sentences.en: get screened for breast cancer.
sentences.zh: 然后提醒女性即将到来的预约。

sentences.en: It would automatically schedule mammograms for staffers
sentences.zh: 筛查就在公司内部进行，

sentences.en: and then remind women about upcoming appointments.
Screenings were conducted right at the company,
so they were easy to get to,
and the wait times were minimal.
In other words,
many of the barriers that keep women from getting tested
sentences.zh: 许多阻碍女性进行检查的障碍

sentences.en: were absent at this company.
Ritesh wanted to find out
how the decisions of women
to get screened for breast cancer
were shaped by information aversion.
sentences.zh: 是如何受到“信息厌恶”影响的。

sentences.en: He obtained detailed information
from the company about employees,
including their health status,
and where they physically sat
in relation to one another.
He discovered that when one staffer
was diagnosed with breast cancer,
sentences.zh: 被诊断出患有乳腺癌时，

sentences.en: this dramatically changed the behavior
of other women who worked in her vicinity.
sentences.zh: 她周围其他女性同事的行为。

sentences.en: We find that, on average,
when a woman is diagnosed with breast cancer,
sentences.zh: 当一名女性被诊断出患有乳腺癌时，

sentences.en: her co-workers, her immediate co-workers,
female co-workers,
reduce their propensity to have a breast screening
sentences.zh: 会降低她们进行乳腺癌筛查的意愿，

sentences.en: in the year in which the diagnosis takes place.
And this impact is persistent
for at least two more years
after the diagnosis for that woman.
Women in the closest proximity
to the woman who was diagnosed with breast cancer
learn of this information.
their willingness to screen falls the moSt.
sentences.zh: 她们筛查的意愿下降得最厉害。

sentences.en: Ritesh found that the severity
of the disease was key.
Women who had a co-worker
diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer
sentences.zh: 被诊断出患有早期乳腺癌的女性，

sentences.en: were less likely to skip their annual screenings.
sentences.zh: 不太可能跳过年度筛查。

sentences.en: But if a woman had a more aggressive case
of breast cancer,
her colleagues were the ones
who were more likely to skip the screenings.
So it appears in our data
that in groups where
the stage of the cancer is late-stage,
sentences.zh: 癌症处于晚期的群体中，

sentences.en: so not an earlier stage of cancer,
sentences.zh: 也就是非早期癌症的情况下，

sentences.en: the avoidance behavior
sentences.zh: 我们观察到的这种回避行为

sentences.en: that we're observing is stronger.
Women who knew a co-worker
who was dying from breast cancer
sentences.zh: 正因乳腺癌而生命垂危的女性，

sentences.en: were the most likely
to skip their mammograMs.
sentences.zh: 跳过她们的乳房X光检查。

sentences.en: Seeing a colleague suffer
may have frightened these women
sentences.zh: 可能让这些女性感到恐惧，

sentences.en: from obtaining information
about their own health.
Not long ago,
I was playing sports
with a friend on a weekend.
I was trying to change directions quickly
when my ankle gave out from under me.
I felt a sharp pain
and collapsed.
In a matter of moments,
my ankle started to swell up.
sentences.zh: 我的脚踝就开始肿胀起来。

sentences.en: It was like watching
a balloon inflate.
I got some ice on the ankle right away,
sentences.zh: 我立刻给脚踝敷了冰块，

sentences.en: but when the pain and swelling
didn't subside
and I found I could put no weight
on the ankle,
I decided I had to go
to the emergency room.
The pain in my ankle
sentences.zh: 朋友开车送我去急诊室时，

sentences.en: as my friend drove me to the ER
was nowhere as bad
as the pain in my head.
Already, I had visions
of needing surgery
and being incapacitated
for a long period of time.
I desperately wanted to believe
my injury wasn't serious.
When I got to the ER,
the triage nurse
took one look
at my ballooned ankle
sentences.zh: 我肿得像气球一样的脚踝，

sentences.en: and told me it was broken.
I argued with her
and told her the pain
wasn't that bad.
When someone took
my blood pressure
and found that it
was high,
I insisted they measure it again
until they got a lower reading.
sentences.zh: 直到测出一个较低的数值。

sentences.en: I didn't think of it
at the time,
but what I was experiencing
was information aversion.
I knew I had hurt myself,
but I didn't want
to know how badly.
As it turned out,
the ankle wasn't broken.
It was just
a very bad sprain.
In the grand scheme of things,
an ankle sprain
is a trivial problem.
It isn't cancer
or heart disease
or a serious infection.
It isn't bankruptcy
or like losing a job.
But it made me realize
sentences.zh: 如果我能对这么小的事情

sentences.en: that if I could experience
information aversion
sentences.zh: 那么当利害关系更大时，

sentences.en: for something so small,
it's hardly surprising
that people experience
much more information aversion
when the stakes are higher.
People who avoid information
rationally know
that they would be better off
if they fully understood
the bad news.
You should always be willing
to hear information
about your finances
or your health.
But deep in the brain,
there are rules
that tell us
to avoid things
that are unpleasant,
painful,
or scary.
Like listeners Jason,
sentences.zh: 那些我们不想听到的消息。

sentences.en: Annie,
and Nancy,
we shut out the news
we'd rather not hear.
If we want people
to pay attention
sentences.zh: 理性的机器人那样行事。

sentences.en: to negative information,
we can't assume
that they will behave
like rational robots.
We have to communicate
information accurately,
but also give people
the capacity
to process and deal
with psychological pain.
Fighting the ostrich effect
means fighting a myth.
Avoiding information
doesn't mean you're a fool.
It means you're human.
